Dr Emma Smiley
Breast Cancer Oncologist
Suite 303
Spirit Breast Clinic
Bullhead St
Suite 303
Bulla


20/5/2019


Re: Mrs Elizabeth Miro , DOB 23/10/1970
Dear Dr Smiley,                                                                                     Commented [PQ1]: Comma required
Thank you for seeing Mrs Elizabeth Miro, a 49-year-old mother-of-three lady mother of three
who is displaying signs and symptoms suggestive of inflammatory breast cancer, for which she
requires urgent evaluation, staging and treatment.
Yesterday, Mrs Miro presented to my clinic with no improvement following a course of oral
flucloxacillin. She stated that she has the same painful and swollen right breast symptoms. On
examination, the erythema has been extended, and pitted skin was observed as well as nipple
retraction . The mammogram and breast ultrasound results shows findings suggestive of               Commented [PQ2]: No space before full stop, please see
malignancy and a deep spiculated mass (4 mm in diameter) in the centre of the right breast was      my comments and explanation below
reported detected . Therefore, an urgent core-needle biopsy was performed and a diagnosis of
inflammatory breast cancer was confirmed.                                                           Commented [PQ3]: Incorrect verb choice

Mrs Miro was initially presented to my clinic on 19/4/2019 complaining of progressive worsening
right breast pain along with swelling, redness, and warmth over the past 3 weeks. On
examination, a mild right breast enlargement and periareolar erythema has been was noticed
with no nipple discharge or retraction. On palpitation her breast was warm, firm, and tender.
Due to the tendrness, tenderness the deep palpitation palpation was limited, however several        Commented [PQ4]: Incorrect word choice / spelling
non-tender lymph nodes was were palpitated palpated in the right axilla. Given that she had
initial diagnosis of possible right-sided mastitis/ inflammatory breast cancer, she was
commenced on antibiotics and a mammogram and breast ultrasound were requested. A follow-            Commented [PQ5]: Article required
up visit was also arranged after one week.
Due to a medical history of right breast lactational mastitis in 2017 and maternal history of
ovarian carcinoma in her mother and breast carcinoma in her aunt who died at the age of 73,
she feels anxious and delayed her second consultation for nearly one month.
I would appreciate it if you could provide Mrs Miro with required care and assistant assistance
as you deem appropriate. Should you require further information, do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,
Dr M.Sh

Overall             This is a good effort Mostafa. The main problem is that it is too long. 300 words instead
                    of 200
Comments            The Name; Address, Date, Salutation and Reference Line are perfect, well done!

                    The address is almost formatted correctly.

                    The correct way to format an address is 1 address line per document line.
                    Dr Emma Smiley
                    Breast Cancer Oncologist
                    Suite 303
                    Spirit Breast Clinic
                    Bullhead St
                    Bulla
                    NSW 2898

                    The word count in the body of the letter is 300 words. Aim for 180-200 in the body of the
                    text. The body of the text starts after the salutation e.g. “Dear Dr. Jones” and ends before
                    a generic closing e.g. “Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any further queries.
                    It does not include the name of the recipient and the date and the address or the sign off
                    e.g. “Yours sincerely,”


                    There are many issues with spaces. Include a space after commas and full stops.
                    INCORRECT
                    Thank you for your help in the matter.Please find test results attached.
                    CORRECT
                    Thank you for your help in the matter. Please find test results attached.
                    INCORRECT
                    The patient,who is suffering from depression,is unable to shower independently.
                    CORRECT
                    The patient, who is suffering from depression, is unable to shower independently.

                    Spelling is mostly good.

                    Verb tenses are mostly good but some errors so please review verb tenses.

                    There are some issues with punctuation, grammar and word choice.

                    Practice proofreading your writing and try to give yourself a few minutes to proofread at
                    the end of the 45 minutes in the exam.

                    Please read the sample letter and compare your letter to it.

                    Review the worksheets in the Grammar and Vocabulary Clinic.

                    Thanks

                    Grade: 320
